title: How To Perform the Infinite Money Glitch in GTA 6
summary: Get infinite money early in GTA 6 with this easy exploit. Play GTA 6 in style with the Recon 70 Pacific Skyline Headset from Turtle Beach.
body_markdown:
Let’s face it: while restrictions in video games can be fun, sometimes you just want to feel like you’re on top of the world, unfettered by the real-world Earthly shackles of needing to earn currency the “legit” way. Why not exploit the system a little bit? I mean who has time for the grind? And it’s a video game anyway —and perhaps the most comprehensive crime simulator ever made— you should be able to do whatever you want!


Well, I’ve got great news for you: there’s already an infinite money glitch that you can find pretty early on in GTA 6, so get to it before it gets patched!


Here’s the few easy steps you need to follow to become an instant infinity-aire:


1. Head to South Vice-Dale. There should be a red, barn-looking warehouse at the point marked on the map.


2. Loot the place.
3. Drive away.
4. Come back — if you drove far enough away, the loot should have completely respawned.
5. Loot the place over and over again, selling whatever you get until you have infinite cash.


That’s it! Now wasn’t that easy?


Well, there are some things to keep in mind:


- It’s a little tedious. It’s pretty safe to say looting and leaving on repeat isn’t the most fun way to earn money in this game.
- Other players might poo poo you for exploiting a glitch. Who cares, I say! It’s your game. But I digress.
- You’ve likely waited 13 whole years since GTA 5 for this game, and you may feel like it’ll cheapen your experience to get extra money like this. Only you can look deep inside your soul to see if you can truly handle being this rich, this early in GTA 6. In other words, your mileage may vary!
- This may get patched out pretty fast. Don’t underestimate the power of Rockstar to google “GTA 6 glitches” and find this one. That said, so long as you don’t update your game, you should be good to glitch away!


After weighing all of the extremely important, heavy moral choices about whether or not to take advantage of some buggy code in a newly released game, you may decide getting your hands on infinite money is worth the while after all. And to that I say: all power (and money) to you.

With a beautiful pastel sunset and palm tree design, you’ll look the part IRL as you drive under the Leonida skyline in the game.


Plus, with a lightweight design for comfortable all-day gaming, flip-to-mute mic, and 40mm speakers for immersive game audio, you’ll be getting a stylish headset with all the fixins that doesn’t break the bank.
